title: Repair a file-processing workflow
goal: Repair a small report script, test failures and preserve a verified rollback.
challenge: Repair the supplied script to validate a readable file of at most 2048 bytes and twenty name|status records, with nonempty names containing no pipe and statuses ok/fail. Report FAIL <name> for failures and a final ok=N fail=N summary. Reject malformed rows/non-files, retain original bytes/mode, publish a report only on success, and prove rollback. Write your own short handover.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' 'app one|ok' 'store\east|fail' 'cache|fail' > checks.txt; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'input=$1' 'grep -F "|fail" "$input" | wc -l' > report.sh
steps.explanation: The supplied script is syntactically valid but does not meet the required format, guards or named evidence. This is synthetic status data, not live services.
steps.expected: Three input rows and a deliberately inadequate script.

steps.command: bash -n report.sh; bash report.sh checks.txt; cp -p report.sh original.sh; sha256sum original.sh > original.sha256; nano report.sh
steps.explanation:
Preserve the faulty original before replacing its three lines. Enter this corrected sixteen-line implementation, save/exit:
#!/bin/bash
if [ "$#" -ne 1 ] || [ ! -f "$1" ] || [ ! -r "$1" ]; then exit 2; fi
[ "$(wc -c < "$1")" -le 2048 ] || exit 2
ok=0; failed=0; n=0
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
  n=$((n+1)); [ "$n" -le 20 ] || exit 4
  case "$line" in *'|'*) ;; *) printf 'missing delimiter\n' >&2; exit 3;; esac
  name=${line%|*}; state=${line##*|}
  case "$name" in ''|*'|'*) printf 'invalid name\n' >&2; exit 3;; esac
  case "$state" in
    ok) ok=$((ok+1));;
    fail) failed=$((failed+1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$name";;
    *) printf "invalid record\n" >&2; exit 3;;
  esac
done < "$1"
printf 'ok=%s fail=%s\n' "$ok" "$failed"
steps.expected: Valid syntax alone did not establish correct behavior.

steps.command: bash -n report.sh; chmod u+x report.sh; timeout -k 2s 5s ./report.sh checks.txt > report.candidate 2> errors.txt; rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then cp -p report.candidate report.txt; else printf 'report refused: %s\n' "$rc"; fi; cat report.txt
steps.explanation: The candidate can be truncated or partial on error. Explicitly guard publication of the final report; do not invent automatic rollback.
steps.expected: FAIL store\east; FAIL cache; ok=1 fail=2.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' stray > bad.txt; timeout -k 2s 5s ./report.sh bad.txt > report.candidate 2> errors.txt; rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then cp -p report.candidate report.txt; else printf 'report preserved, status=%s\n' "$rc"; fi; sha256sum -c original.sha256
steps.explanation: A malformed record must not replace the valid published report. The candidate/error may change; retain that evidence.
steps.expected: Status 3 and previous final report preserved; original still matches.

steps.explanation: Write observed fault, exact repair, success/error evidence, limitations and rollback. This is your report, not a placeholder self-assessment.
steps.expected: A short supported handover; no app inspection or score.

steps.command: cp -p report.sh corrected.sh; cp -p original.sh report.sh; cmp original.sh report.sh; timeout -k 2s 5s ./corrected.sh checks.txt > repeated.txt; cmp report.txt repeated.txt
steps.explanation: Retain the corrected script, restore the original faulty script/metadata, and verify both rollback and reproducible corrected output.
steps.expected: Original restored, corrected report still reproducible.

hints: Which evidence distinguishes valid syntax, correct behavior and safe publication?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
review: I retained the stated observations and can explain the outcome.
I checked failure cases and preserved originals; my review is not an application-verified score.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 105.2; 103.1/103.4/103.7/103.8 reinforcement. Reinforcement is labeled; no full-objective mastery. Completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
